script.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Papa claims to have seen how many coins some Macedonians had. He was not there, and the passage gives no such detail.
“MANY cents more” invents a specific kind and quantity of gift. Paul says they gave beyond their ability, not how many coins they gave.
“Nobody begs to carry a burden” is an untrue blanket claim, so the comparison does not hold.
The closing line turns the verse into a generic, preachy maxim about everything lining up.
The explanation is flat and generic: it repeats the answer without adding a distinct insight or Papa's personality.
It identifies the Macedonians as the example Paul uses to test the Corinthians' love. Paul mentions their eagerness earlier, but does not explicitly identify the “others” here.
“The others are the Macedonians” states an identification the verse leaves open.
After quoting the verse, the explanation simply repeats the answer. It is generic rather than adding insight or Papa's voice.
The half-done batch joke repeats the same idea and punchline used in stop 1, card 9, answer 1.
Saying the other side “kicks back” adds an unsupported picture of the people receiving relief as idle.
The explanation only quotes the verse and restates equality as things being even. It is generic and adds no distinct insight or personality.
“Corinth isn't left empty” asserts something Paul does not say. He says the others' surplus will meet the Corinthians' need in turn.
